title: Tetralogy of Fallot
summary: Build TOF from one malaligned septum, then read its signs, treat a tet spell, plan surgery and dodge the PYQ traps.
closing: One malaligned septum, a narrowed infundibulum, a right ventricle working against it: hold that picture and every TOF question follows from it.

objectives.text: Choose the four components of classic TOF and the fifth that makes the pentalogy, and reject ASD, PDA and LVH as members of the four.
Trace the causal chain from the infundibular obstruction to blood bypassing the lungs and a secondary right ventricular hypertrophy.
Predict whether a child with TOF is blue or a 'pink Tet' from RVOT versus systemic resistance, and tell 'most common cyanotic CHD' from 'usually presents as a cyanotic neonate'.
Pick the auscultation that fits TOF: a harsh ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border, an inaudible P2, and a murmur that softens in a spell.
Predict the TOF ECG and chest X-ray from right ventricular load and low pulmonary flow, treating the boot-shaped heart as a 'may classically' sign.
Choose echocardiography as the diagnostic gold standard and match CT and MRI to the extra job each does.
Order the steps of tet-spell management, bedside measures first, and name the lever each one pulls (systemic resistance, pulmonary vasodilation, RV filling).
Time complete repair for a well infant and pick what the Blalock-Taussig shunt connects.
Pick pulmonary insufficiency as the commonest reason for reoperation after repair and recognise the lifelong arrhythmia, sudden-death and endocarditis risks.
Rank the causes of death in unrepaired TOF, with hypoxic spells first.
Choose the TOF associations and figures (right aortic arch, 22q11.2 deletion, incidence) and say where sources disagree.
Tell the PYQ key from the current source where they diverge (age qualifier, boot shape in infants, palliation for high-risk infants, imaging limits) and answer both.

traps.trap: ASD, PDA or LVH is part of the four classic components of TOF (or a true component is picked as the 'NOT' answer)
The RVOT obstruction is purely valvular, and RVH is a primary defect (or the cause) rather than a consequence
Pentalogy of Fallot adds something other than an ASD (PDA, a second VSD)
The boot-shaped heart is always or usually present in TOF, or is caused by the LV or a large pulmonary artery
Confusing the TOF radiograph with other cyanotic CHD signs, or expecting increased pulmonary vascularity
'Most common cyanotic CHD' with the age qualifier dropped or reversed
Every TOF is cyanotic from birth; acyanotic 'pink Tets' are missed
During a tet spell the murmur gets louder
Knee-chest position (squatting) works by lowering PVR or raising pulmonary flow directly, not by raising systemic vascular resistance
Tet spell management starts with drugs or intubation; positioning and oxygen are skipped
Spells are treated like heart failure (inotrope, diuretic, fluid restriction) or by lowering afterload
Catheterisation, CT or MRI is the gold standard for diagnosing TOF
Echo, CT and MRI are interchangeable; echo needs no adjunct, or MRI is first-line
ECG and chest X-ray in TOF show left-sided changes (LVH, left axis, plethora, cardiomegaly)
P2 is loud or S2 widely split in TOF
Down syndrome (or another syndrome) is the usual TOF association, or 22q11.2 deletion is in most cases
Incidence figures and right aortic arch frequency confused
Complete repair is neonatal for all, or delayed to school age; a BT shunt is the routine first step
The Blalock-Taussig shunt joins the aorta (or a vein) to the pulmonary artery, or is the definitive repair
The commonest late problem or reoperation reason after repair is residual VSD, recurrent PS or LV failure, not pulmonary insufficiency
Repaired TOF is cured: no arrhythmia, sudden death or endocarditis risk
Leading cause of death in unrepaired TOF is brain abscess, stroke or heart failure; the 68/17/13 shares are swapped

segments.title: A blue baby and a list that doesn't add up
segments.goal: Open on a cyanotic infant, have the learner name the most common cyanotic CHD (P12) and attempt a 'which is NOT a component' stem (P01 surface) before any teaching, so the component gap is felt.

prefer.reason: The component list is the module's backbone error; letting the learner fail the 'which is NOT' stem first makes the rebuild in S2 land.

segments.title: Four from one septum
segments.goal: Rebuild the four components from one anteriorly malaligned VSD, place the obstruction at the infundibulum and RVH at the end of the chain, then add the ASD that makes the pentalogy (P01, P04, P05, P06; associations P31, P33 in a deeper branch).

prefer.reason: Each component follows from the previous one, so a ladder of small causal steps rebuilds the set from logic rather than a list (E2 and E3 repair).

segments.title: Pink or blue, and what you hear
segments.goal: Use a pink-Tet vignette to establish cyanosis as RVOT versus systemic resistance, then fix the auscultation: harsh ejection murmur, inaudible P2, and a murmur that softens in a spell (P14, P15, P28, P16).

prefer.reason: The spell murmur is a reversed-mechanism trap; predicting the murmur change before seeing K29 is the repair the trap map asks for.

segments.title: ECG, film and the test that confirms
segments.goal: Derive the right-sided ECG and the oligaemic, boot-shaped film from RV load and low pulmonary flow, then place echo, CT and MRI on a ladder by the question each answers (P27, P30, P08, P11, P24, P25).

segments.title: Managing a tet spell
segments.goal: In a spell case, the learner picks the first step, the lever behind knee-chest positioning and the reason for fluids, and recognises a softening murmur as a spell (P17, P18, P20, P22, P19).

prefer.reason: A first-step vignette is the PYQ form for spells and lets every later step arrive as feedback on the learner's call.

segments.title: Surgery and the years after
segments.goal: Time complete repair for a well infant, name the BT shunt connection, then pick pulmonary insufficiency, lifelong arrhythmia risk and hypoxic spells as the leading killer without surgery (P35, P37, P39, P41, P43).

segments.title: PYQ traps, keys and the current source
segments.goal: Re-test the anatomy, sign, test and surgery traps in PYQ form, teaching both key and current source behind the warning sign where they diverge (P07, P09, P10, P12b, P13, P29, P32, P34, P36, P38, P44).

prefer.reason: This segment is built from pattern.md keys and the note's Exam notes; a rapid drill with 'teach both' feedback fits it directly.

segments.title: Put TOF back together
segments.goal: The learner rebuilds the take-home with cold probes: the four components, the spell sequence, the test ladder and the after-repair legacy (P03, P02, P21, P23, P26, P40, P42).

prefer.reason: Ordering the spell steps and choosing the true statements is the re-test form the trap map assigns to TR10 and TR20.
